correctness.rationale: For every cyclic band with n>=3,k>=2 its bipartite graph is connected, so the reduced row/column incidence has rank 2n-1. The projection KKT strict-complementarity region has Jacobian Q=I-B^T(BB^T)^{-1}B extended by zero. Translation reduces rows to the k shifts. A standard-library exact rational Gauss–Jordan checker exhausts all 440 orbit rows for n=3..13 and verifies unique n13 width7 excess 99556468/14256211151; full support has product centering projection norm 4(1-1/n)^2. Separately exact rational primal feasibility and complementary multipliers verify finite positive-input attainment with t=1/1000. Universal large-n or arbitrary-support extrapolations are not claimed.

value.rationale: Cyclic consecutive bands are a natural structured family of constrained doubly stochastic support patterns, useful for locality-limited matching and bistochastic smoothing. The theorem identifies a sharp finite order at which removing permitted entries increases the endpoint sensitivity above unrestricted complete support; this distinguishes Hilbert contractivity from coordinatewise robustness. The cutoff is a complete natural finite classification with an exact KKT-realized perturbation, not an arbitrary isolated rational constant or a routine renaming. It can guide stability analysis of sparse assignment relaxations and reveals a nonmonotonic support effect.
